Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.7; MLA.PC.FA.1

Function A is f(x)=x². Function B is a degree 3 polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Which comparison is correct

answer.text: Function A has no minimum, and Function B has both ends up.

feedback.text: This misreads both functions. The quadratic has a minimum, and an odd-degree polynomial has opposite end behavior.

answer.text: Function A is degree 3, and Function B must have a maximum.

feedback.text: This confuses the degree of Function A and assumes a maximum from degree alone.

answer.text: Function A has a minimum, and Function B has opposite end behavior.

feedback.text: Correct. A quadratic opening upward has a minimum, and an odd-degree polynomial with positive leading coefficient falls left and rises right.

answer.text: Function A and Function B must have the same end behavior.

feedback.text: Different degree and leading-coefficient structures can produce different end behavior.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.2; MLA.PC.FA.3

A polynomial model has factor (x-6), and x represents time in seconds. What does x=6 mean if it is valid in context

answer.text: The y-intercept is 6.

feedback.text: A y-intercept occurs when x=0, not when a factor equals zero.

answer.text: The maximum value is 6.

feedback.text: A zero identifies an input where the output is 0, not a maximum value.

answer.text: The model has degree 6.

feedback.text: A factor showing x=6 as a zero does not determine the full polynomial degree.

answer.text: The modeled quantity is 0 at 6 seconds.

feedback.text: Correct. The factor (x-6) gives a zero at x=6, meaning the output is 0 at that time.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.4; MLA.PC.FA.5

Which statement correctly identifies restrictions for f(x)=sqrt(x-2) and g(x)=1/(x+5)

answer.text: f excludes x=2, and g requires x>=-5.

feedback.text: The radical endpoint x=2 is allowed, and rational restrictions are excluded values, not interval domains.

answer.text: f requires x>=2, and g excludes x=-5.

feedback.text: Correct. The radical needs x-2>=0, and the rational denominator cannot equal 0.

answer.text: f requires x<=2, and g excludes x=5.

feedback.text: The radical inequality is reversed, and the rational exclusion has the wrong sign.

answer.text: f allows all real numbers, and g excludes no values.

feedback.text: Both functions have restrictions from their structures.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.8; MLA.PC.FA.9

Let f(x)=x+3 and g(x)=2x. Which expression correctly represents f(g(x)) and uses composition rather than addition

feedback.text: This is (f+g)(x), not f(g(x)).
This multiplies the functions rather than composing them.
This is g(f(x)), not f(g(x)).
Correct. f(g(x)) means substitute 2x into f, giving 2x+3.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.10; MLA.PC.FA.11

A function h(t) gives height from time, and T(h) gives temperature from height. If an inverse function reverses inputs and outputs, what does T(h(t)) represent

answer.text: temperature from time

feedback.text: Correct. Height is found from time first, then temperature is found from that height.

answer.text: time from temperature

feedback.text: This describes reversing the relationship, not the given composition.

answer.text: height from temperature

feedback.text: This reverses the input-output direction of the temperature function.

answer.text: temperature plus height

feedback.text: Composition uses one function output as another function input; it is not addition.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.12; MLA.PC.FA.13

Why might f(x)=x² be restricted to x>=0 before using its inverse in a distance model

answer.text: The restriction removes all possible inputs.

feedback.text: The domain still includes all nonnegative inputs.

answer.text: The restriction changes the function into a logarithmic model.

feedback.text: A domain restriction does not change a quadratic into a logarithmic function.

answer.text: The restriction makes all outputs negative.

feedback.text: Restricting to x>=0 does not make outputs negative; x² remains nonnegative.

answer.text: The restriction makes the function one-to-one and supports meaningful nonnegative inputs.

feedback.text: Correct. Restricting to one side makes the inverse a function and can match a nonnegative context such as distance.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.EX.1; MLA.PC.EX.2

Which statement connects y=200(1.05)t and log base 1.05 of 2

answer.text: The model is linear, and the logarithm gives an output value directly.

feedback.text: The model is exponential, and the logarithm asks for an exponent.

answer.text: The model shows 5 percent decay, and the logarithm has no connection to exponents.

feedback.text: The factor 1.05 shows growth, and logarithms are inverse to exponential relationships.

answer.text: The model shows 105 percent decay, and the logarithm asks for a base.

feedback.text: This misinterprets the growth factor and the role of a logarithm.

answer.text: The model shows 5 percent growth, and the logarithm asks what exponent on 1.05 gives 2.

feedback.text: Correct. A factor of 1.05 represents 5 percent growth, and logarithms answer exponent questions.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.MOD.1; MLA.PC.MOD.2

A system solution is (4,9). A Piecewise rule says use f(x)=2x+1 for x>=4. Which statement is correct

answer.text: The system graphs are parallel, and the Piecewise rule uses x<4.

feedback.text: A given solution means the graphs intersect, and x=4 belongs to x>=4.

answer.text: The system graphs intersect at (4,9), and f(4)=9 uses the x>=4 rule.

feedback.text: Correct. A system solution is an intersection, and x=4 is included in x>=4.

answer.text: The system has no solution, and f(4) cannot be evaluated.

feedback.text: The ordered pair is a solution, and the Piecewise interval includes x=4.

answer.text: The system solution is only a y-intercept, and f(4)=8.

feedback.text: A system solution is a shared point, and 2(4)+1=9.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.4; MLA.PC.FA.8; MLA.PC.FA.9

Let f(x)=sqrt(x) and g(x)=x-7. What domain condition is needed for f(g(x))

answer.text: x>=7

feedback.text: Correct. f(g(x))=sqrt(x-7), so x-7 must be nonnegative.

answer.text: x<7

feedback.text: This would make x-7 negative, which is not allowed inside the square root.

answer.text: x cannot equal 7

feedback.text: The input x=7 is allowed because the radicand is 0.

answer.text: all real numbers

feedback.text: The square root in the composition creates a domain restriction.

Question ID: PC_U01_PRE_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.7; MLA.PC.EX.1; MLA.PC.MOD.2

Which comparison correctly interprets f(x)=100(0.8)² and a Piecewise model that is constant at 100 for x<0

answer.text: f is quadratic, and the Piecewise model must be used for every x-value.

feedback.text: The first model is exponential, and Piecewise rules depend on intervals.

answer.text: f shows decay, and the Piecewise rule applies only on its stated interval.

feedback.text: Correct. The factor 0.8 is decay, and Piecewise rules must be matched to their intervals.

answer.text: f has no key features, and the Piecewise model cannot be compared.

feedback.text: Both models have interpretable features and constraints that can be compared.

answer.text: f shows growth, and the Piecewise model has no interval restriction.

feedback.text: A factor less than 1 shows decay, and the Piecewise rule applies only for x<0.\
